newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH SHIPPING FIRM ATTRACTS FOREIGN INVESTORS.
newsitem.headline: POLISH SHIPPING FIRM ATTRACTS FOREIGN INVESTORS.

text.p: Three foreign companies want to buy a majority stake in Polish state-owned shipping firm Transocean SA, the sale of which is likely to be completed next year, the company's president said on Tuesday.
Janusz Gadek told Reuters the interested investors were Greek company Lascardis Shipping, U.S. transport firm Eastwind and Dannish-British, Luxemburg-based fuel firm DSS.
"Lascardis, Eastwing and DSS are interested in buying a majority share package of Transocean and its management supports the option," Gadek said.

He said the treasury ministry, which controls 100 percent of shares in Transocean, would soon launch a tender for an adviser on the company's privatisation and complete the sell-off in the first half of 1998.
Transocean, based in the Baltic port of Szczecin, operates eight ships and owns 68 trucks with licences for international shipments.
The company's net profit is expected to fall to 46,000 zlotys in 1997 from last year's 173,600 zlotys.
